land.text: Chang'an and the Guanzhong prefectures, taken when the Tang emperor fled on 8 January 881

predecessors.note: The rebellion itself began in 874 (Wang Xianzhi and Shang Junzhang at Changyuan) and Huang Chao sacked Guangzhou in 879; the Qi holds land only from the fall of Chang'an.

land.text: Chang'an, which Li Keyong entered in summer 883 as Huang fled east

successors.note: Huang Chao was killed in Langhu Valley (Laiwu, Shandong) on 13 July 884; no land was held after the summer of 883.

capitals.name: Chang'an (Xi'an)
capitals.note: The page does not name a capital but has Huang move into the Tang palace in Chang'an and declare the Qi there.

rulers.name: Huang Chao (Emperor of Qi)
rulers.title: emperor of Qi
rulers.note: Infobox reign 16 January 881 to 13 July 884; era name Jintong (881-884) on the Huang Chao page.

correction.text: Chang'an and the Guanzhong prefectures held by the Qi from the Tang emperor's flight on 8 January 881 to Li Keyong's entry in summer 883, including Tong and Hua prefectures until Zhu Wen's defection in autumn and winter 882

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 881 (reviewer ea-04-x split at the 882 losses). The pages name Chang'an, Tong Prefecture (under Zhu Wen) and Hua Prefecture as Qi holdings and four circuits (Heyang, Pinglu, Hezhong, Zhongwu) as submitted but later returned to Tang; no page draws a frontier, so Guanzhong is the researcher's reading, and the 882 losses shrink it (ledger). Neither page gives an area; the only figures are troops (a Qi army of 150,000 in spring 883).

correction.text: Chang'an and the Guanzhong prefectures still held by the Qi after Zhu Wen surrendered Tong Prefecture to the Tang 'by fall 882' and Hua Prefecture followed 'by winter 882', until Li Keyong's entry in summer 883

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 882-883 (reviewer ea-04-x split): the 882 loss of Tong and Hua prefectures (the Weinan 70 km circle, about 18,000 of the 60,000 km2 Guanzhong reading) is taken out, so the keyframes carry the ledger's 882 loss. The pages draw no frontier.

ledger.note: 881: Huang Chao takes Chang'an and founds the Qi. 'The emperor fled on January 8, 881, and Huang's forces entered the city that day'; he then 'declared himself the emperor of a new state of Qi' (infobox reign from 16 January 881).

region.text: Chang'an and the prefectures around it

ledger.note: 881: the Qi holds Guanzhong. Huang's forces occupy Chang'an and the Guanzhong prefectures around it (Tong Prefecture under the Qi governor Zhu Wen is named for 882); Zheng Tian of Fengxiang resisted. The region is the researcher's reading of the prefectures named. Mirror of the Tang loss of January 881.

region.text: Tong and Hua prefectures, east of Chang'an on the road to Tongguan (both lie in modern Weinan; the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 882: Zhu Wen changes sides. 'Zhu Wen, Qi governor of Tong Prefecture, surrendered to Tang' in fall 882 and Hua Prefecture followed in winter 882; the Tang ledger has no mirror gain (a gap on the Tang side).

region.text: Chang'an and what remained of the Qi's Guanzhong

ledger.note: 883: Li Keyong retakes Chang'an. He 'joined Tang forces in winter 882, defeated a 150,000-man Qi army in spring 883, and entered Chang'an in summer 883'; Huang fled east. Mirror of the Tang gain of 883.

region.text: Langhu Valley in modern Laiwu, Shandong, where the remnant of Huang's army ended

ledger.note: 884: Huang Chao dies. His nephew Lin Yan killed Huang and his family on 13 July 884 in Langhu Valley (Laiwu, Shandong); the New Book of Tang gives suicide instead. The Qi had held no land since summer 883.

wars.name: Huang Chao Rebellion
wars.outcome: Tang victory in 884: Li Keyong, Zhu Wen and others retake Chang'an in 883 and Huang is killed on 13 July 884.
wars.note: Infobox 874-884, result Tang victory. Huang crossed the Yangzi in 878, took Guangzhou in autumn 879 and reached Tan Prefecture (Changsha) by winter 879 before turning north; those raids held no land.

certainty.note: A rebel zone with no frontier on any page; Tong and Hua prefectures pass back to the Tang in 882.

sources.title: Huang Chao
sources.note: Infobox reign 16 January 881 to 13 July 884, the Qi proclamation in Chang'an's palace, the four submitting circuits, Li Keyong's entry (summer 883), death in Langhu Valley.

sources.title: Huang Chao Rebellion
sources.note: Chang'an on 8 January 881, Zhu Wen's defection (fall 882) and Hua Prefecture (winter 882), Li Keyong's spring and summer 883, the march of 878-879, the 874 start.

notes: Rebel state written for ea-04-x (no Cliopatria row). Open points: (1) Luoyang and Tong Pass fell in the winter of 880 but neither page gives a month or says how long Qi held Luoyang, so no Luoyang event is recorded; (2) the four circuits of Zhuge Shuang (Heyang), Wang Jingwu (Pinglu), Wang Chongrong (Hezhong) and Zhou Ji (Zhongwu) 'submitted to Qi' and returned to Tang without dates, so no vassal pair is drawn; (3) the 882 Tong and Hua losses have no Tang mirror; (4) the Huang Chao page gives the proclamation as 881 and the era Jintong, the rebellion page gives no era name; (5) the Tang dossier's counterpart string 'Qi (Huang Chao)' is this state, slug qi-huang-chao. Gazetteer: Tong and Hua prefectures are drawn with a Weinan circle; no 'Tongguan' or 'Huayin' place exists.
